specAnchors.text: understand experiments that can be used to investigate reaction rates by: i an initial-rate method, carrying out separate experiments where different initial concentrations of one reagent are used A ‘clock reaction’ is an acceptable approximation of this method. ii a continuous monitoring method to generate data to enable concentration-time or volume-time graphs to be plotted

primer.text: Continuous monitoring collects concentration data throughout a reaction rather than at a single moment. This note walks the iodination of propanone followed by colorimetry: building a calibration curve from standard iodine solutions, mixing measured volumes, logging absorbance against time, and reading the rate at any instant as the gradient of a tangent.

modules.title: Watching the whole reaction: colorimetric monitoring
modules.opening: Continuous monitoring collects data across the entire reaction instead of one moment. The showcase is iodine's decolourisation during propanone iodination in acid: a calibration curve converts colorimeter absorbance into iodine concentration, and the logged readings trace the whole concentration-time curve.
keyPoints: Continuous monitoring collects experimental data throughout the reaction so a full concentration-time graph can be plotted.
In the iodination of propanone, catalysed by dilute sulfuric acid, brown iodine decolourises as it forms iodopropanone and hydrogen iodide.
A colorimeter reads absorbance, and absorbance scales with how concentrated the coloured species is.
Before the run, absorbances of standard iodine solutions are measured to build a calibration curve for converting readings into concentrations.
Four burettes hold 0.02 mol dm-3 iodine, 1.0 mol dm-3 propanone, 1.0 mol dm-3 sulfuric acid and distilled water, so volumes can be varied while the total stays constant.

low.restatement: Calibrate first with standard iodine solutions, mix measured volumes, start the timer as iodine joins, and log absorbance throughout.
low.analogy: Fitting a backstage translator (the calibration curve) before the show, so every applause meter reading (absorbance) converts into audience numbers (concentration).
low.examPointer: Name the calibration curve's job explicitly: absorbance in, concentration out.

medium.restatement: Because iodine is the only strongly coloured species, its absorbance is a live read-out of [I2]; the calibration curve anchors the scale so numbers, not just shapes, come out.
medium.analogy: A fuel gauge calibrated before the drive: the needle's position only means something once you know what empty and full are.
medium.examPointer: The iodine beaker is added last because adding it starts the reaction - mixing order is timing order.

modules.title: Volumes, results and rates at any instant
sourceHeadings: Specimen Results Table for the Iodination of Propanone
modules.opening: The specimen tables show the run's design and its output: volume recipes for each mixture, then logged iodine concentrations against time. A tangent at any chosen moment converts the curve into an instantaneous rate, demonstrated at 300 seconds.
keyPoints: The volume compositions table lists burette volumes for each run, with distilled water keeping the total constant.
The specimen results table and its graph record iodine concentration falling through the reaction.
A practical tip: choose the filter giving the strongest absorbance, the complementary colour to the solution's own.
The rate at any point comes from drawing a tangent and finding its gradient.
At 300 seconds the tangent's gradient is 0.0069/590 = 1.17 x 10^-5 mol dm-3 s^-1.

low.restatement: The results table feeds the concentration-time curve; a tangent at any chosen time gives that instant's rate by gradient.
low.analogy: A marathon split chart: pick any checkpoint, measure the local pace, and that pace is the rate at that moment.
low.examPointer: For tangent marks, quote the rise and the run, then the units mol dm-3 s^-1.

medium.restatement: Continuous data let you interrogate any instant, which is exactly what order analysis needs: gradients at several times reveal how rate responds to the falling concentration.
medium.analogy: A flight recorder: rather than one number for the whole journey, every moment is recoverable.
medium.examPointer: The complementary-colour filter rule earns marks in practical-write-up questions.

glossary.definition: Collecting concentration data throughout a reaction to plot a full concentration-time graph.
A plot of absorbance against concentration for standard solutions, used to convert readings into concentrations.
The small receptacle holding the sample inside the colorimeter.

workedExample.prompt: On the specimen results graph, draw a vertical line from the 300 s mark up to the curve and add the tangent there. The tangent falls 0.0069 units over a run of 590 units. Find the rate of reaction at 300 seconds.
steps: Apply the gradient formula to the tangent: rise divided by run.
workedExample.finalAnswer: The rate at 300 s is 1.17 x 10^-5 mol dm^-3 s^-1.
